originalGit.acquisition: Read-only depth-1 blobless no-checkout clone and all available branch-tree metadata. No upstream script executed; no branch merged; Luke origin preserved.
originalGit.changedDuringAudit: First refs listing returned nine heads; a tenth cursor/mission-climate-2608 head appeared by clone. This is a pinned snapshot, not a standing claim about future branches.

terrainSummary.citation: Barker, M. K., et al. (2023), A New View of the Lunar South Pole from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter, The Planetary Science Journal, https://doi.org/10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1. LOLA DEM LDEM_80S_80MPP_ADJ, NASA GSFC PGDA product 90, https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/90.
terrainSummary.coordinateReference: MOON_ME / DE421 sphere, radius 1737400 m, south-polar stereographic metres. +X toward east longitude 90°, +Y toward east longitude 0°. Row 0 is the maximum-Y side. originX and originY are the centre of pixel (0,0).
terrainSummary.preparationNote: Windowed read with rasterio and GDAL /vsicurl/ from the cloud-optimized GeoTIFF. Analysis heights are the native 80 m postings, rounded to 0.01 m, with no spatial resampling. The display hillshade is a separate 2x2 block mean and is not this grid. Horizon search radius is 12000 m; the window keeps that radius inside the grid for every example site.
terrainSummary.nodataPolicy: Source nodata is NaN. This window has no nodata. Missing mask azimuths are never filled as flat.

integrationNotes: All inventoried branches share the same blobs for the listed terrain/ephemerides/sites/demo manifest.
Original numeric terrain grid is 432×432, 80 m spacing, 12 km ray radius around three derived example sites, not global terrain.
Preview PNG is 160 m display hillshade and explicitly not numerical analysis terrain.
Original Earth Blue Marble/cloud textures have NASA credits; static cloud mosaic is not selected-date weather.
No GLB/glTF model is present in any inventoried original branch; procedural spheres with NASA textures are not NASA-authored mesh assets.
Original app source code has no licence file located in these trees; do not infer redistribution rights from NASA imagery credit.
Do not import original science/UI blindly: preserve current canonical science contracts and validate adapters independently.
